incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: spike in 5xx and gateway timeouts for /v1/generate and /v1/chat in prod-us-east. 5m error rate = 12.4%, p95 latency x3 normal. Paging oncall.
Mateo (oncall): I'm up. Looking at overviews now. Marking P1 until we scope customer impact.
Claire: Grafana snapshot: scheduler_ring-7 and scheduler_ring-9 queue_depth jumped simultaneously. ring-9 head_wait median ~13s, some sessions >30s. batch_size distribution shifted right (peak batches ~160).
Arjun: KV prefetch latency also spiked ~4x around same time. Seeing redis RESP latencies and occasional connection retries on kvcache nodes. Could be causing batching to stall while waiting on prefixes.
Priyanka (cs): Multiple enterprise customers reporting 504s for chat. They
 like an ETA and whether wee seeing data loss.
Mateo (oncall): ETA estimate 10-15m for visible recovery after mitigations. No indication of lost requests yet; gateway timeouts likely client-facing symptoms.
SRE Helper: Quick logs from scheduler-9: 
```
[scheduler-9] WARN batch_queue: enqueue_count=158 head_wait=18.6s
[worker-3] ERROR dispatch: dispatch_deadline_exceeded batch_id=0x2ab4
[gateway] WARN upstream: 504 write timeout to runtime
```
Mateo (oncall): Suggest immediate protective steps: 1) reduce max_batch_wait to 6ms on affected rings, 2) reduce max_batch_tokens from 256->128, 3) enable ingress backpressure to cap per-tenant qps, 4) spin up extra worker pods for ring-9. Any objections?
Claire: +1. Also add short-lived head-of-line eviction for sessions waiting > 10s to free slots.
Arjun: I'll check KV cluster health and start cordon/drain if a node shows IO issues. In parallel, we should disable background KV prefetch to lower pressure.
Deploy Bot: No scheduler/batching deploys in last 2h. Latest deploys were to tokenizer service ~50m ago.
Priyanka (cs): Please share ETA for customers. They want a rough time window and whether wee applied fixes.
Mateo (oncall): Applying runtime changes now to ring-9 and ring-7. Command: 
```
PATCH https://runtime-api.prod/v1/schedulers/ring-9/config
{ "max_batch_wait_ms": 6, "max_batch_tokens": 128 }
```
Mateo (oncall): Response: 200 OK. Applying to ring-7.
SRE Helper: Scaling workers: `kubectl scale deploy worker-ring-9 --replicas=10 -n prod-us-east` -> OK.
Claire: Enabling head eviction via runtime lua script on scheduler nodes: 
```
/opt/runtime/bin/evict_long_waiters --threshold-seconds=10 --action=evict_to_fallback
```
Arjun: Running quick health on kvcache cluster: node-12 IO latency high (iostat showing high await). Starting drain: `kubectl drain node-12 --ignore-daemonsets` and cordon.
SRE Helper: Disabled KV prefetch on runtime flagged nodes: `runtime toggle kvcache_prefetch false` -> OK.
Claire: Monitoring queue_depth: ring-9 160 -> 98 within 2m. Error rate dropping: 12.4% -> 7.1%. p95 latency 2.1s -> 1.0s.
Priyanka (cs): Sending interim note to customers: "We've applied rate-limiting and batching changes and are scaling workers. Expecting recovery within ~10 minutes. We will follow up with a detailed post-incident update"
Mateo (oncall): Good. Also start temporary routing: divert 25% new /v1/generate requests to lighter model variant to reduce heavy-kernel pressure in region.
Deploy Bot: Routing rule applied: `edge-toggle --route /v1/generate --to canary-lite --weight 25` -> OK.
Arjun: Node-12 drain complete; redis latency improved to baseline. ring-9 queue_depth now 98 -> 34 over next 4m. Error rate down to 2.4%.
Claire: p95 now 380ms, gateway 504s almost gone. Keeping reduced batch settings for 20m and watching.
Priyanka (cs): Customers updated. No SLA breaches flagged yet but monitoring.
Mateo (oncall): Next steps (postmortem items): 1) root-cause KV node IO sensitivity and add auto-evacuation on IO > 80%, 2) implement per-session head_eviction for >12s wait, 3) revisit default batch sizing for bursty traffic, 4) add ingress adaptive throttles per-tenant. Assigning: Arjun -> KV auto-evacuation + canary; Claire -> head_eviction design; Mateo -> postmortem + customer timeline; Priyanka -> customer communication log.
SRE Helper: Adding a temporary alert rule: if queue_depth > 90 for > 90s -> auto-scale workers and reduce batch window via runbook. Creating alert now.
Mateo (oncall): We'll keep this channel open 30m for observation. If error rate stays <3% and p95 <500ms for 20m, we'll resolve.
Deploy Bot: Incident metadata pinned: runbook -> https://runbooks.redwood/incidents/batching-hol, grafana -> https://grafana.redwood/d/xyz/scheduler-queues
incident-bot: Incident acknowledged by Mateo (oncall). Severity: P2 (escalated -> monitoring).
